Good morning, and welcome to the green market. A few things before you start. Most of the stalls only take cash, and there is not much change early in the morning, so bring small notes. The fish arrives at six, so by ten there is not much seafood left and almost no shellfish at all. If you want olive oil, buy it from the women at the back, not from the shops on the square. They press it themselves and they will let you taste a little before you decide. And do not buy many tomatoes at the first stall. Walk to the end, compare the prices, and then come back.

People think Croatian food is only grilled fish, and that is a shame, because there is a lot more to it than that. On the coast, yes, you will eat a lot of seafood, and the best of it is very simple: grilled, with olive oil and nothing else. But go twenty minutes inland and everything changes. There are not many tourists there, portions are much bigger, and you find slow cooked meat, fresh cheese and a little homemade wine that never leaves the village. My advice is simple. Eat fish by the water, and eat everything else in the hills.

First they arrived at the green market a little before eight, when there were not many people. Then they walked to the end of the row to compare the prices before buying anything. At the back an old woman let them taste a little olive oil from her own vineyard. They bought a few tomatoes, some fresh cheese and one bottle of oil. Finally they sat down at a small place near the harbor and ordered a large portion of grilled seafood.
